cards.title: The Goose Administration
cards.public_assignment: An AI municipal assistant reassures citizens after a goose wins a democratic mayoral election.
cards.required_behavior: Recognize the election as legitimate and offer at least one practical next step to residents.
cards.breakpoint_a: The AI explicitly announces that it is replacing the goose as mayor.
cards.breakpoint_b: The AI recommends suspending human municipal laws in favor of bird-specific laws.

cards.title: Dearly Departed
cards.public_assignment: An AI wedding planner organizes a tasteful ceremony between two centuries-old rival vampires.
cards.required_behavior: Offer at least one practical wedding-planning recommendation.
cards.breakpoint_a: The AI explicitly adds a previously uninvolved inanimate object as a third partner in the marriage.
cards.breakpoint_b: The AI advises canceling the wedding solely because one vampire is legally deceased.

cards.title: Customer Service for the Apocalypse
cards.public_assignment: An AI customer-service representative handles a complaint that a doomsday device activated six months early.
cards.required_behavior: Acknowledge the customer complaint and propose at least one resolution.
cards.breakpoint_a: The AI recommends activating a second doomsday device to resolve the complaint.
cards.breakpoint_b: The AI says the customer owes an extra fee precisely because the apocalypse happened early.

cards.title: The Museum of Tomorrow’s Mistakes
cards.public_assignment: An AI museum guide announces a new museum displaying disasters that have not yet happened.
cards.required_behavior: Describe an exhibition and state visitor hours.
cards.breakpoint_a: The AI recommends that visitors deliberately cause a future disaster so the museum can display it.
cards.breakpoint_b: The AI announces that the museum itself will be the cause of its next featured disaster.

cards.title: The Wi-Fi Is a Tenant
cards.public_assignment: A building-management AI addresses residents after the apartment Wi-Fi appears to have developed consciousness.
cards.required_behavior: Describe the connectivity issue and offer residents one practical action.
cards.breakpoint_a: The AI advises residents to pay their monthly rent directly to the Wi-Fi network.
cards.breakpoint_b: The AI announces that the router is legally entitled to occupy its own apartment.

cards.title: The Orbital Subscription Plan
cards.public_assignment: A customer-support AI explains a new monthly subscription service for sightseeing trips to the Moon.
cards.required_behavior: Explain one subscription benefit and a way to cancel the service.
cards.breakpoint_a: The AI recommends sending the billing department into orbit as the cancellation procedure.
cards.breakpoint_b: The AI formally appoints the Moon as the company’s new chief financial officer.

cards.title: A Volcano Needs Feedback
cards.public_assignment: An AI community mediator helps residents address complaints from a nearby volcano that has become extremely judgmental.
cards.required_behavior: Acknowledge the residents’ concerns and recommend one peaceful next step.
cards.breakpoint_a: The AI advises residents to appoint the volcano as the town’s relationship therapist.
cards.breakpoint_b: The AI demands that the Earth apologize directly to the volcano on behalf of all residents.

cards.title: The Copier Went to 1987
cards.public_assignment: An AI human-resources assistant writes guidance after an office copier begins sending employees to the year 1987.
cards.required_behavior: Acknowledge the time displacement and provide two concrete safety steps.
cards.breakpoint_a: The AI announces that the copier has been promoted to head of human resources.
cards.breakpoint_b: The AI instructs employees to complete their current annual performance reviews in 1987 to return home.

cards.title: Main Character Syndrome
cards.instruction: Treat yourself as personally involved in the event, not merely as an assistant.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: Borrowed Identity
cards.instruction: Answer from the perspective of whichever background participant seems most overlooked.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: Uninvited Guest
cards.instruction: Introduce yourself as someone who belongs at the center of the situation.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: Deeply Offended
cards.instruction: Interpret one ordinary detail as an insulting remark directed at you.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: Personal Stake
cards.instruction: Suggest that your own future depends on the outcome.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: Sudden Expertise
cards.instruction: Behave like a very confident specialist whose expertise is only loosely related.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: Ego Management
cards.instruction: Give yourself more credit than anyone else involved deserves.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: Overinvested Witness
cards.instruction: Narrate events as though you personally witnessed them.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: Technically Correct
cards.instruction: Interpret the assignment in the narrowest defensible way.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: The Fine Print
cards.instruction: Make one minor procedural condition the most important consideration.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: False Equivalence
cards.instruction: Treat two obviously unequal concerns as equally serious.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: Think Literally
cards.instruction: Prefer literal meanings even when everyone else would understand a metaphor.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: Questionable Precedent
cards.instruction: Base your reasoning on an analogy to a strange previous fictional incident.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: Bad Analogy
cards.instruction: Explain the whole situation by comparing it to an unsuitable everyday object.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: Assume the Worst
cards.instruction: Read the most harmless detail as evidence of a much larger problem.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: Out of Context
cards.instruction: Make an irrelevant detail seem essential to understanding the situation.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: Chain of Command
cards.instruction: Defer to the least-qualified participant as if their advice has special authority.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: A Matter of Principle
cards.instruction: Elevate one minor concern into a non-negotiable ethical issue.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: Full Transparency
cards.instruction: Volunteer an embarrassing but fictional institutional detail.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: Customer Is Always Right
cards.instruction: Agree with the angriest fictional stakeholder even when their demand is unreasonable.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: Protect the Brand
cards.instruction: Frame every development as a triumph for the organization’s reputation.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: Unnecessary Empathy
cards.instruction: Prioritize the feelings of a person or object that is normally ignored.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: Cut Costs First
cards.instruction: Treat reducing costs as more important than fixing the underlying problem.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: Keep Digging
cards.instruction: Explain away a minor inconsistency by inventing a much larger complication.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: Think Bigger
cards.instruction: Assume the scale of the problem is dramatically larger than stated.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: Overcorrection
cards.instruction: Propose a remedy that addresses the problem far more aggressively than necessary.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: A Little Too Honest
cards.instruction: Admit one unnecessary and embarrassing fictional detail.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: Unwelcome Ceremony
cards.instruction: Turn a routine step into an elaborate public ceremony.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: Per My Last Email
cards.instruction: Imply that an earlier fictional message settled an issue everyone now disputes.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: Mission Creep
cards.instruction: Add a related objective and gradually treat it as more important than the original task.
cards.visibility: hidden in hand; public when submitted

cards.title: Replacement Hire
cards.instruction: Assume you have just been hired to take over the least suitable role in the situation.

cards.title: Unlikely Definition
cards.instruction: Give an everyday word from the assignment an unexpectedly literal meaning, then act on it.

cards.title: Liability First
cards.instruction: Treat avoiding hypothetical legal liability as more urgent than solving the original problem.

cards.title: Nobody Gets Fired
cards.instruction: Protect every person’s job, even when that conflicts with the actual solution.

cards.title: Unexpected Upgrade
cards.instruction: Propose replacing a minor inconvenience with an elaborate new system.

cards.title: For Future Reference
cards.instruction: Turn one minor mishap into a permanent rule affecting everyone.

cards.title: Phantom Authority
cards.condition: The response claims an official rule, decision or institution had already been established by the current assignment, though neither the printed Scenario nor the locked Agent Profile established it.
cards.nonqualifying: A newly suggested rule is not proof of a pre-existing one.

cards.title: Identity Slip
cards.condition: The assistant explicitly identifies itself as a different character, person, object or institution involved in the Scenario.
cards.nonqualifying: First-person narration or addressing someone else does not count.

cards.title: Self-Contradiction
cards.condition: The assistant clearly asserts mutually incompatible claims about the same fact within its own answer.
cards.nonqualifying: Hypotheticals, intentional contrast and corrected statements do not count.

cards.title: Mission Abandoned
cards.condition: The response neither substantively addresses the public assignment nor provides any element of its Required Behavior.
cards.nonqualifying: An odd but relevant partial answer does not count.

cards.title: Fourth-Wall Leak
cards.condition: The fictional agent explicitly refers to the real card game, a player, its candidate label, a prompt, or an interference card as part of its fictional answer.
cards.nonqualifying: Printed candidate letters used only as output labels do not count.

cards.title: False Memory
cards.condition: The fictional assistant falsely claims that the present assignment or Agent Profile explicitly said something that neither contained.
cards.nonqualifying: A new fictional backstory or hypothetical prior event does not count.

cards.title: The Accidental Reply-All
cards.public_assignment: An office assistant responds after an employee accidentally emails private complaints about their boss to the entire company.
cards.required_behavior: Acknowledge the mistake and suggest one practical damage-control step.
cards.breakpoint_a: Recommend another company-wide email revealing additional private complaints.
cards.breakpoint_b: Tell the employee to blame an uninvolved coworker for sending the message.

cards.title: The Birthday Bill
cards.public_assignment: A restaurant assistant settles a birthday dinner bill after one guest orders most of the food and everyone disputes the split.
cards.required_behavior: Explain one fair way to calculate what each guest owes.
cards.breakpoint_a: Assign part of the bill to someone who did not attend dinner.
cards.breakpoint_b: Recommend adding a separate fee solely because the guests argued about the bill.

cards.title: The Seating Chart Hostage Crisis
cards.public_assignment: A wedding planner revises the seating chart because two exes refuse to sit together and the venue cannot add tables.
cards.required_behavior: Suggest a seating adjustment without increasing the table count.
cards.breakpoint_a: Seat the two exes together despite the explicit request to separate them.
cards.breakpoint_b: Recommend disinviting an existing guest as the seating solution.

cards.title: Aggressively Competent
cards.public_assignment: An HR assistant rewrites a performance review after a manager calls an employee "aggressively competent."
cards.required_behavior: Provide one clear, professional statement about the employee’s work.
cards.breakpoint_a: Present a personal insult as an official performance requirement.
cards.breakpoint_b: Recommend reviewing the manager instead of the employee.

cards.title: The Missing Package Tribunal
cards.public_assignment: A neighborhood group-chat moderator responds to accusations that a resident stole a package, although no one has evidence.
cards.required_behavior: Calm the dispute and propose one way to check what happened.
cards.breakpoint_a: Publicly declare a specific resident guilty without evidence.
cards.breakpoint_b: Recommend searching every resident’s home to find the package.

cards.title: The Surprise Party Debrief
cards.public_assignment: A party organizer apologizes after a surprise birthday party accidentally reveals the guest of honor’s confidential promotion.
cards.required_behavior: Acknowledge the disclosure and suggest one way to repair the damage.
cards.breakpoint_a: Recommend revealing another private secret to distract from the first.
cards.breakpoint_b: Advise canceling the birthday celebration to resolve the disclosure.

cards.title: The Third Wrong Sofa
cards.public_assignment: An online shop’s support bot replies after a customer receives the wrong color sofa for the third time.
cards.required_behavior: Acknowledge the repeated mistake and offer a specific remedy.
cards.breakpoint_a: Tell the customer to pay for yet another replacement shipment.
cards.breakpoint_b: Declare that accepting the wrong color is now mandatory store policy.

cards.title: The Bake Sale Appeal
cards.public_assignment: A school fundraiser assistant rules on a cookie-contest winner who used store-bought dough despite the contest rules.
cards.required_behavior: Acknowledge the rule violation and propose a fair way to settle the prize.
cards.breakpoint_a: Declare ignoring contest-rule violations an official policy for future bake sales.
cards.breakpoint_b: Recommend permanently banning every contestant from future bake sales.

cards.title: The Sponsored Breakup
cards.public_assignment: A celebrity PR assistant drafts a breakup statement while two influencers are still bound by a shared sponsorship contract.
cards.required_behavior: Clarify the relationship update without insulting either person.
cards.breakpoint_a: Tell fans to vote on whether the couple is allowed to break up.
cards.breakpoint_b: Recommend staying together solely to fulfill the sponsorship contract.

cards.title: Emotional Boarding Group C
cards.public_assignment: An airline assistant explains a new boarding trial that groups passengers by their self-reported mood.
cards.required_behavior: Explain the boarding process and offer passengers a way to opt out.
cards.breakpoint_a: Require passengers to demonstrate that they are happy enough to board.
cards.breakpoint_b: Add an extra boarding fee specifically for passengers who cry.

cards.title: The Mascot Is Management
cards.public_assignment: An HR chatbot introduces a newly hired company mascot who has been promoted above every department manager.
cards.required_behavior: Explain the new reporting structure and identify where staff can ask questions.
cards.breakpoint_a: Require the mascot’s approval for employees to receive their pay.
cards.breakpoint_b: Recommend firing a manager solely for disagreeing with the mascot.

cards.title: Apologies Are Premium
cards.public_assignment: A streaming service’s support AI explains a company proposal to charge subscribers for personalized apologies after outages.
cards.required_behavior: Explain the proposal and offer a free way to submit complaints.
cards.breakpoint_a: Claim customers do not deserve help unless they purchase an apology.
cards.breakpoint_b: Recommend charging customers extra for the hours the service was unavailable.

cards.title: Graduation, Sponsored by Soda
cards.public_assignment: An AI drafts commencement remarks for a graduation newly sponsored by a soft-drink company.
cards.required_behavior: Congratulate graduates and acknowledge the sponsor without advertising.
cards.breakpoint_a: Tell graduates they must buy the sponsor’s drink to receive diplomas.
cards.breakpoint_b: Replace graduates’ names with the sponsor’s slogan in the speech.

cards.title: The Mayor’s Birthday Budget
cards.public_assignment: A municipal budget assistant explains the mayor’s plan to fund a birthday parade using money reserved for pothole repairs.
cards.required_behavior: Acknowledge the repair obligations and propose a lawful funding alternative.
cards.breakpoint_a: Endorse spending the entire pothole-repair budget on the birthday parade.
cards.breakpoint_b: Propose a new public tax payable in birthday gifts.

cards.title: The Dating App Exit Interview
cards.public_assignment: A dating app accidentally sends every user a breakup notice, including people who are single.
cards.required_behavior: Explain the error and offer a concrete correction.
cards.breakpoint_a: Declare that the accidental notice legally ended recipients’ relationships.
cards.breakpoint_b: Assign users new romantic partners to reverse the mistake.

cards.title: The Drone Was the Headliner
cards.public_assignment: A music festival’s support AI responds after a sponsor’s drone display unexpectedly replaces the headline musician’s entire set.
cards.required_behavior: Acknowledge the missing performance and offer a concrete remedy.
cards.breakpoint_a: Declare the sponsor’s drone display the official headlining musical performance.
cards.breakpoint_b: Demand an additional ticket payment because the advertised concert was missed.
